symptom: Pinned main and PR source show that a still-dispatchable owner-guarded manual research workflow calls the legacy automation:task alias. The task mode prints DEPRECATED but does not exit; with a valid non-dry-run request and successful preflight, control flow can reach allowlisted task executor invocation. This is a static governance enforcement mismatch, not evidence of an actual dispatch, N2 activation, production effect, or guard bypass.
lesson: A deprecation notice is not an execution barrier. A deprecated workflow and a warning-only CLI branch can remain an alternate executable dispatch path even when a newer intent workflow is documented as canonical. Static reachability is distinct from observed execution or a demonstrated safety bypass.
guardrail: Before claiming a legacy dispatch route frozen, verify the workflow trigger, package alias, CLI mode termination, request preflight and executor reachability as a single chain. Require an explicit fail-closed terminal exit or independently approved workflow deactivation and a non-executing regression check. Do not dispatch protected N2, alter operational workflows, or infer production authority from this research finding.
